learning_outcomes.text: Understand the key concepts and aspects in the field of building air conditioning and in refrigeration and freezing chambers.
Apply knowledge to the calculation of thermal loads and air conditioning systems using established methods.
Apply knowledge to develop designs that meet specific requirements determined by the technical building code for building air conditioning.
Select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods in the field of building air conditioning with mechanical compression air conditioning systems and freezing chambers.
Evaluate the environmental impact of air conditioning systems in the building sector and refrigeration and freezing chambers.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
Adequate knowledge of their engineering branch that includes some cutting-edge knowledge in their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and carry out experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory skills.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component, or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet the required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply current legislation as well as mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards in the field of mechanical engineering.
Knowledge and ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions, and to apply environmental and sustainability technologies.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
Applied knowledge of thermal engineering.

syllabus_topics: Thermal loads. Refrigeration and freezing installations. Regulations. Technical Building Code. Regulation on Thermal Installations in Buildings. Energy in buildings. Energy demand and energy consumption. Energy certification of buildings.
Mechanical compression. Vapor compression cycle. Cascade and double compression cycles. Heat pumps. Refrigeration. Devices of mechanical compression machines.
Air conditioning systems. Types of air conditioning systems. Psychrometry. Analysis of air conditioning systems.
teaching_methods: Problem-solving in class with student participation
Visit to the university's air conditioning facilities
Computer lab and experimental practices: Practice execution and report presentation
